chunks: It was said: What you have mentioned is not correct, because doubt regarding the miracle that appears on the hand of the Imam is not a defect in knowing him for the general public in a general sense. Rather, it is a defect in whether what is generally known and whose knowledge is valid is this specific person or not. And doubt in this is not disbelief, because if it were disbelief, it would be disbelief even if the miracle does not appear, for surely before the appearance of this miracle in his hand, there is one who doubts about him, and it is permissible for him to be the Imam and for another to be so as well. Rather, the defect in the knowledge obtained by him in a general sense is if he doubts in the future regarding his Imamate in a general sense, and that is what prevents it from occurring from him in the future.
ai.seo_question: Is doubting the identity of the Imam considered disbelief in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Al-Tusi clarifies that doubt regarding the specific identity of the Imam is not disbelief (Kufr) because it is a temporary state of uncertainty that existed prior to the manifestation of the miracle, distinguishing it from the certainty of the Imamate itself. He argues that while general knowledge of the Imamate remains valid, specific identification is subject to probabilistic reasoning, and only doubt in the future occurrence of the Imamate would constitute a fundamental defect in belief.
